summary: Synchronized retry/backoff misalignment causing persistent 429s during orchestrated bulk flush
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses affecting bulk flush jobs run by their orchestrator after a brief 5xx spike. Impact: Several scheduled nightly bulk-inspect flush jobs fail with 429s for 15-40 minutes, causing downstream reconciles to backlog and retry. Environment: StreamlineAI running Dedicated (enterprise) pool in prod-us-east. Pattern observed: 429s begin ~5 minutes after orchestrated job starts, persist in waves, and correlate with synchronized retry loops from many workers. Customer-facing impact: increased latency for nightly indexing jobs and missed data windows.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer schedules a 5000-file bulk flush across 200 workers via their orchestrator.
2) Workers start concurrently and perform preflight checks (HEAD requests + health probes) and then POST multipart uploads to /v1/embeddings.
3) A short origin-side 5xx spike occurs (approx 30s), triggering worker retry logic.
4) Worker retry policy is fixed-interval retry with minimal jitter (0.5s) causing retries to re-synchronize.
5) After initial retries, tenant experiences repeated 429s for ~20-35 minutes until refill window drift and manual intervention.
logs:
Selected excerpts (redacted keys): 
- 2026-03-10T02:14:21Z worker-17 POST /v1/embeddings -> 502 (orig)
- 2026-03-10T02:14:22Z worker-17 retry#1 -> 502
- 2026-03-10T02:14:23Z worker-17 retry#2 -> 429 (rate-limit)
- 2026-03-10T02:14:25Z many-workers: 429 flood begins (rate-limiter: tenant_token_exhausted)
- 2026-03-10T02:22:10Z rate-controller epoch-swap detected: refill-offset=+5s (note: dedicated pool refill alignment changed during autoscaler activity)
- 2026-03-10T02:33:50Z customer orchestrator backoff logs show fixed_sleep=0.5s, jitter=0.1s
- 2026-03-10T02:45:01Z support command: temporarily paused orchestrator; gradual recovery observed within 15 minutes
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: synchronized retries from many workers amplified a small 5xx window into a tenant-level token exhaustion. Observed contributing factors: 1) Customer retry policy uses short fixed backoff with insufficient jitter, enabling lock-step retries. 2) Dedicated pool refill window misalignment after recent autoscaler activity caused refill offsets across edge and origin -> soft refill drift. 3) Healthcheck/preflight requests from orchestrator are counted against tenant quota and exacerbated token depletion. 4) No isolated burst pool configured for long-running bulk jobs. Evidence: correlated timestamps between worker retry spikes and rate-limiter 'token_exhausted' events in origin logs; rate-controller epoch-swap log directly preceding prolonged 429 window. Mitigations tried: customer applied temporary pause + staggered restart which allowed natural smoothing; support temporarily bumped tenant burst allowance (manual) which accelerated recovery.
customer_comments: 2026-03-10T03:02:12Z — Emily Park (StreamlineAI): We saw our nightly flush fail for 3/5 cycles and then self-recover after we manually paused workers and restarted them in staggered batches. Can you explain why retries turned into a full tenant throttle?

2026-03-10T03:45:00Z — Aisha Thompson (Support): We're seeing synchronized retry waves amplify a transient 5xx and the rate-controller refill offset likely extended the exhaustion window. We're investigating and will propose configuration changes.
2026-03-11T09:10:55Z — Emily Park: We don't have a per-route burst pool for these bulk endpoints; how quickly can we get a safer config?
support_comments: 2026-03-10T03:20:11Z — Marco Ruiz (SRE): Captured origin and edge refill logs. Confirmed epoch swap + refill offset. Recommending immediate changes: 1) switch to exponential backoff with jitter on client side; 2) configure a split burst pool for /v1/embeddings route for their org; 3) exempt healthchecks from quota counting if possible.

2026-03-11T10:02:00Z — Support Team: Opened a config change PR on customer's Dedicated control plane to add a temporary burst policy and healthcheck exemption. PR: https://github.com/streamlineai/ingest-orch/pull/78 (customer-side) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/432 (Redwood-side policy flag).

2026-03-12T14:30:34Z — Marco Ruiz: Pulled rate-limiter metrics; post-config change we see peak token pressure reduced by ~72% for the next scheduled run. Need to validate across 3 runs before marking resolved.
resolution: Workaround applied: temporary tenant burst lift + customer staggered restart. Permanent recommended fixes: 1) Client-side: adopt exponential backoff with randomized jitter (base=200ms, multiplier=2, max=10s) and limit retry attempts for idempotent bulk writes; 2) Server-side: create isolated burst pool for long-running bulk ingest routes and add healthcheck exemption toggles for Private/Dedicated customers; 3) Align refill windows between edge and origin during autoscaler events — implement epoch-swap smoothing (PR #432). Deployment notes: rate-limiter PR staged to canary for Dedicated pools; customer confirmed improved behavior after canary enabled.
next_steps:

- Ops: Add automated check in Dedicated onboarding to suggest route-level burst pools when large bulk schedulers are detected (owner: Leah Chen). Target discovery ticket created: INT-2026.
